   263	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   264	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   265	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin
   266	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   267	-/
   268	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   269	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   270	  let lineEdges :=
   271	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   272	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   273	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   274	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   275	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   276	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   277	  let basisEdges :=
   278	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   279	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   280	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   281	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   282	  let pairEdges :=
   283	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   284	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   285	  let msEdges' :=
   286	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   287	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   288	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   289	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'
   290	
   291	/-- A Pauli question is a type together with a full ambient coefficient vector
   292	(`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   293	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   294	-/
   295	abbrev PauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliType × PauliSpace P
   296	
   297	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
   298	the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`; it is Lean-only
   299	infrastructure for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   300	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   301	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   302	-/
   303	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   304	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   305	
   306	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   307	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   308	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   309	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
   310	-/
   311	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   312	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   313	  simp [pauliEdges]
   314	
   315	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   316	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   317	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
   318	-/
   319	noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   320	    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   321	  by
   322	    classical
   323	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   324	    exact
   325	      Distribution.map
   326	        (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
   327	        (fun s =>
   328	          ((s.1.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
   329	            (s.1.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))
   330	
   331	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
   332	the seven answer forms in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint lines 331-367,
   333	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   334	-/
   335	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   336	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   337	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   338	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   339	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   340	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   341	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   342	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   343	  deriving DecidableEq
   344	
   345	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   346	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   347	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   348	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   349	-/
   350	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   351	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   352	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   353	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   354	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   355	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   356	
   357	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   358	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   359	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   360	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   361	-/
   362	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   363	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   364	  toFun
   365	    | .value a => .inl a
   366	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   367	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   368	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   369	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
   370	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   371	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   372	  invFun
   373	    | .inl a => .value a
   374	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   375	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   376	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   377	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   378	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
   379	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
   380	  left_inv := by
   381	    intro x
   382	    cases x <;> rfl
   383	  right_inv := by
   384	    intro x
   385	    cases x with
   386	    | inl a => rfl
   387	    | inr x =>
   388	        cases x with
   389	        | inl a => rfl
   390	        | inr x =>
   391	            cases x with
   392	            | inl a => rfl
   393	            | inr x =>
   394	                cases x with
   395	                | inl a => rfl
   396	                | inr x =>
   397	                    cases x with
   398	                    | inl a => rfl
   399	                    | inr x =>
   400	                        cases x with
   401	                        | inl a => rfl
   402	                        | inr a => rfl
   403	
   404	noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fintype (PauliAnswer P) :=
   405	  Fintype.ofEquiv (PauliAnswerCode P) (pauliAnswerEquiv P).symm

   410	/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
   411	fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
   412	self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
   413	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   414	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   415	-/
   416	noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
   417	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   418	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   419	  fixedBinTrace P.model
   420	    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
   421	
   422	/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
   423	`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   424	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   425	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   426	-/
   427	noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   428	  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
   429	    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)
   430	
   431	/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
   432	well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   433	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   434	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   435	-/
   436	def validPauliAnswer {P : AdmissibleParams} (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   437	  match t, a with
   438	  | .point _, .value _ => true
   439	  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   440	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   441	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   442	  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   443	  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   444	  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   445	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   446	  | _, _ => false
   447	
   448	/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   449	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   450	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   451	-/
   452	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   453	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   454	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   455	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   456	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   457	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   458	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   459	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   460	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   461	
   462	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   463	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   464	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   465	-/
   466	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   467	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   468	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   469	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   470	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   471	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   472	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   473	
   474	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   475	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   476	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   477	-/
   478	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   479	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   480	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   481	
   482	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   483	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   484	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   485	-/
   486	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   487	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   488	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   489	    (match W with
   490	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   491	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   492	
   493	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   494	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   495	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   496	-/
   497	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   498	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   499	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   500	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   501	      (a * (match W with
   502	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   503	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   504	
   505	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   506	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   507	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   508	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   509	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   510	-/
   511	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   512	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   513	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   514	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   515	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   516	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   517	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   518	
   519	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   520	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   521	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   522	-/
   523	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   524	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   525	  open Classical in
   526	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   527	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   528	      if tA = tB then
   529	        decide (a = b)
   530	      else
   531	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   532	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   533	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   534	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   535	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   536	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   537	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   538	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   539	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   540	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   541	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   542	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   543	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   544	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   545	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   546	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   547	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   548	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   549	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   550	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   551	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   552	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   553	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   554	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   555	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   556	          else true
   557	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   558	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   559	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   560	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   561	          else true
   562	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   563	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   564	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   565	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   566	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   567	    else false
   568	
   569	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   570	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   571	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   572	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   573	-/
   574	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   575	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   576	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   577	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   578	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   579	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   580	  μ_prob := by sorry
   581	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   582	
   583	end
   584	
   585	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Pauli basis test soundness
     5	
     6	The quantitative error function and the source-shaped soundness statement live
     7	here.  All analytic estimates are intentionally proof-level obligations in the
     8	stage-4.1 skeleton; the carriers below are concrete finite-dimensional vectors
     9	and matrices so that later proofs can use the existing Hilbert-space API.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The main declaration is `thm:pauli` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, with paper origin
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    16	The distance functionals use `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` from
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    25	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    26	
    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    30	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    31	as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`,
    32	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    33	-/
    34	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    35	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    36	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    37	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    38	
    39	/-- Matrix conjugation by a finite-dimensional linear isometry.  This is a
    40	Lean-only helper for the operator conclusion of `thm:pauli`; it uses the
    41	matrix representation of the isometry and its conjugate transpose.  Blueprint
    42	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    43	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    44	-/
    45	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    46	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    47	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    48	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    49	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
    50	  U * M * Uᴴ
    51	
    52	/-- Reindex a finite Euclidean-space vector along an equivalence.  This is the
    53	coordinate form of the tensor-register shuffle used in the paper's ideal
    54	state (`def:EPR`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`),
    55	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
    56	-/
    57	noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    58	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    59	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
    60	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    61	    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))
    62	
    63	/-- Coordinate tensoring of two local maps on a bipartite state.  The formula
    64	is a genuine finite sum over the input coordinates; preservation of the norm
    65	is part of the later soundness proof for `thm:pauli`, blueprint
    66	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    67	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    68	-/
    69	noncomputable def isometryTensor
    70	    {ιA ιB ιA' ιB' R : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    72	    [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA'] [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    73	    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    74	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × R))
    75	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × R))
    76	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    77	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) :=
    78	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) ℂ).symm
    79	    (fun p =>
    80	      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
    81	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × R) ℂ)
    82	            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
    83	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιB' × R) ℂ)
    84	            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *
    85	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA × ιB) ℂ) ψ (i, j)) )
    86	
    87	/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
    88	ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from
    89	`def:EPR` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper
    90	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
    91	-/
    92	noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    93	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    94	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    95	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    96	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    97	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
    98	      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    99	    (fun p =>
   100	      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
   101	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
   102	          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
   103	
   104	/-- The Pauli question carrying no additional coefficient data, as in
   105	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
   107	-/
   108	def pauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P :=
   109	  (.pauli W, 0)
   110	
   111	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and
   112	B-side registers.  This is a concrete matrix form of the operator comparison
   113	in `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper
   114	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
   115	-/
   116	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   117	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   118	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   119	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   120	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   121	  fun p q =>
   122	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
   123	      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
   124	    else 0
   125	
   126	/-- The symmetric B-side ideal Pauli projector from `thm:pauli`, blueprint
   127	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   128	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   129	-/
   130	noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   131	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   132	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   133	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   134	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   135	  fun p q =>
   136	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
   137	      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2
   138	    else 0
   139	
   140	/-- Lift a conjugated A-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   141	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   142	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   143	-/
   144	noncomputable def liftedAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   145	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   146	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   147	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   148	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   149	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   150	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   151	  fun p q =>
   152	    if p.2 = q.2 then
   153	      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
   154	    else 0
   155	
   156	/-- Lift a conjugated B-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   157	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   158	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   159	-/
   160	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   161	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   162	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   163	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   164	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   165	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   166	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   167	  fun p q =>
   168	    if p.1 = q.1 then
   169	      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
   170	    else 0
   171	
   172	/-- A finite witness packaging the auxiliary dimensions, isometries, and state
   173	from `thm:pauli`.  This structure is a Lean-only encoding of the existential
   174	data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
   175	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   176	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   177	-/
   178	structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   179	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   180	  ιA' : Type
   181	  ιB' : Type
   182	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   183	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   184	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   185	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   186	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   187	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
   188	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   189	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
   190	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   191	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   192	
   193	attribute [instance] PauliSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype
   194	  PauliSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
   195	
   196	/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
   197	conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
   198	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   199	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   200	-/
   201	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
   202	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   203	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   204	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   205	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   206	        ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   207	      pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   208	
   209	/-- The symmetric B-side operator-distance quantity from `def:povm-distance`,
   210	blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   211	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   212	-/
   213	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceB
   214	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   215	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   216	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   217	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedBEffect S w.φB
   218	        ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   219	      pauliProjOnB'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   220	
   221	/-- `thm:pauli`: every sufficiently successful Pauli basis test strategy admits
   222	local isometries and an auxiliary unit state for which the state and both
   223	operator families are close at scale `deltaQld`.  The theorem uses the
   224	once-and-for-all self-dual-normal field model selected by `fixedFieldModel` for
   225	each admissible size, rather than a freshly quantified field identification.
   226	Blueprint
   227	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper origin
   228	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   229	
   230	The paper's asymptotic constants are encoded by the explicit `deltaQld`
   231	functional; the squared operator distances use the quantitative convention of
   232	`def:povm-distance` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`).
   233	-/
   234	theorem pauli_soundness :
   235	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   236	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   237	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   238	          ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
   239	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤

     4	/-!
     5	# The Magic Square game
     6	
     7	The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
     8	question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
     9	Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
    10	carrier is needed here.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, from
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    20	
    21	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    22	
    23	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    24	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 188-203, paper origin
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    26	-/
    27	inductive MsType where
    28	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    29	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    30	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    31	
    32	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    33	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    34	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    35	-/
    36	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    37	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    38	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    39	
    40	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    41	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`; paper
    42	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    43	-/
    44	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    45	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    46	
    47	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    48	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    49	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    50	-/
    51	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    52	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    53	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    54	
    55	/-- The Magic Square incidence graph has an edge, as required by the
    56	nonempty-support API of `graphDistribution`.  This is the finite carrier fact
    57	used to instantiate `def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    58	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    59	-/
    60	theorem msEdges_nonempty : msEdges.Nonempty := by
    61	  refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.constraint 0) (.var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
    62	  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(0, 0), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
    63	
    64	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    65	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    66	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    67	-/
    68	inductive MsAnswer where
    69	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    70	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    71	  deriving DecidableEq
    72	
    73	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    74	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    75	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    77	-/
    78	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    79	
    80	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
    81	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    82	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    83	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
    84	-/
    85	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    86	  toFun
    87	    | .triple β => .inl β
    88	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    89	  invFun
    90	    | .inl β => .triple β
    91	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    92	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
    93	  right_inv := by
    94	    intro x
    95	    cases x <;> rfl
    96	
    97	noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
    98	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm
    99	
   100	instance : Inhabited MsAnswer := ⟨.bit 0⟩
   101	
   102	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
   103	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 188-203; paper
   104	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`).
   105	-/
   106	def msWinPredicate :
   107	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   108	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   109	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   110	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   111	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   112	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   113	      decide
   114	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   115	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   116	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   117	      decide
   118	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   119	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   120	  | _, _, _, _ => false
   121	
   122	/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
   123	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
   124	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
   125	-/
   126	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   127	  QuestionA := MsType
   128	  QuestionB := MsType
   129	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   130	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   131	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty
   132	  μ_prob := by sorry
   133	  decide := msWinPredicate
   134	
   135	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
  toFun
    | .pointVals a => .inl a
    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
  invFun
    | .inl a => .pointVals a
    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
  right_inv := by
    intro x
    cases x with
    | inl a => rfl
    | inr x =>
        cases x with
        | inl a => rfl
        | inr a => rfl

instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩

noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm

/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val

/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
  match t, a with
  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
  | _, _ => false

/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j

/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j

/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
  open Classical in
  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
        match tA, tB, a, b with
        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
        | _, _, _, _ => true
      else false

/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
  μ_prob := by sorry
  decide := ldWinPredicate P

end

/-!
# The low-degree game

This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
the ambient coefficient space; their conditional-linearity and distribution
invariants are recorded as proof-level obligations for later stages.

## References

The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
`def:ld-win-predicate` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`; their paper origin is
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

noncomputable section

/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
`def:ld-game` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
structure LdParams where
  q : ℕ
  m : ℕ
  d : ℕ
  k : ℕ
  hm : 1 ≤ m
  hd : 1 ≤ d
  hk : 1 ≤ k
  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
  hdvd : m ∣ q

/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility
view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified
parameter.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq

/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.
Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K

/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
inductive LdType where
  | point
  | aline
  | dline
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype

/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
-/
abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m

/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
-/
abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P

/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))

/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
  z (.inl (.inr ()) )

/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
  fun i => z (.inr i)

/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))

/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j

/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
  fun i => match i with
  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
  | .inr _ => 0

/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
-/
noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
  fun i => match i with
  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
  | .inr _ => 0

/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
-/
noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
  let rep := lineRepMap direction
  fun i => match i with
  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
  | .inr j => direction j

/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
  | .point => ldPointCL P
  | .aline => ldALineCL P
  | .dline => ldDLineCL P

/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is a named
Lean proof obligation for the prose assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`,
blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
  sorry

/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is the
level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
  sorry

/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
-/
abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P

/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
  Distribution.map
    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
    (fun s =>
      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))

/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`; paper
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
-/
inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
-/
abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))

/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint

/-!
# The Magic Square game

The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
carrier is needed here.

## References

This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, from
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
-/

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 188-203, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
-/
inductive MsType where
  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
  | var (j : Fin 9)
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype

/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
-/
def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩

/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`; paper
origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
-/
def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0

/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
-/
def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))

/-- The Magic Square incidence graph has an edge, as required by the
nonempty-support API of `graphDistribution`.  This is the finite carrier fact
used to instantiate `def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
-/
theorem msEdges_nonempty : msEdges.Nonempty := by
  refine ⟨Sym2.mk (.constraint 0) (.var (msConstraintVars 0 0)), ?_⟩
  exact Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨(0, 0), Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩

/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
-/
inductive MsAnswer where
  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
-/
abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2

/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
-/
noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
  toFun
    | .triple β => .inl β
    | .bit γ => .inr γ
  invFun
    | .inl β => .triple β
    | .inr γ => .bit γ
  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
  right_inv := by
    intro x
    cases x <;> rfl

noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm

instance : Inhabited MsAnswer := ⟨.bit 0⟩

/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 188-203; paper
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`).
-/
def msWinPredicate :
    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
      decide
        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
      decide
        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
  | _, _, _, _ => false

/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:512-610`.
-/
noncomputable def msGame : Game where
  QuestionA := MsType
  QuestionB := MsType
  AnswerA := MsAnswer
  AnswerB := MsAnswer
  μ := graphDistribution msEdges msEdges_nonempty
  μ_prob := by sorry
  decide := msWinPredicate

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-!
# The Pauli basis test

This file supplies the finite question and answer alphabets, the typed
conditionally-linear question sampler, and the Boolean win predicate for the
Pauli basis test.  The quantitative soundness theorem is isolated in
`Soundness.lean`.

## References

The source-facing nodes are `def:admissible`, `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
and `def:pauli-win-predicate` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-367`; their paper origin is
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:908-1225`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT

noncomputable section

/-- The numerical admissible Pauli-test parameter package.  Its scalar carrier
uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel q hq`, so the paper's fixed
self-dual-normal identification is not quantified in the test statement.  This
is `def:admissible` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
structure AdmissibleParams where
  q : ℕ
  m : ℕ
  d : ℕ
  hd : 1 ≤ d
  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
  hdvd : m ∣ q

/-- The positivity of the ambient dimension is a proof obligation implicit in
the admissibility convention `def:admissible`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
theorem AdmissibleParams.one_le_m (P : AdmissibleParams) : 1 ≤ P.m := by
  sorry

/-- The fixed model accessor for an admissible parameter package.  It is a
compatibility view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently
quantified field representation.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`; paper
origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
noncomputable def AdmissibleParams.model (P : AdmissibleParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq

/-- The low-degree parameter view of an admissible Pauli-test package.  This is
a Lean-only bridge supporting the statement closure; it is not an additional
hypothesis of `thm:pauli`.  Blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
def AdmissibleParams.toLdParams (P : AdmissibleParams) : LdParams where
  q := P.q
  m := P.m
  d := P.d
  k := 1
  hm := P.one_le_m
  hd := P.hd
  hk := by decide
  hq := P.hq
  hdvd := P.hdvd

/-- The scalar carrier associated with an admissible parameter package.  It is
the globally fixed field carrier selected by `AdmissibleParams.model` in
`def:admissible`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
-/
abbrev PauliScalar (P : AdmissibleParams) := P.model.K

/-- The six families of Pauli-test questions.  This is part of
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
inductive PauliType where
  | point (W : PauliKind)
  | aline (W : PauliKind)
  | dline (W : PauliKind)
  | pauli (W : PauliKind)
  | pairW (W : PauliKind)
  | pair
  | ms (t : MsType)
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype

/-- The register blocks used by the Pauli question space.  These are the
coordinates displayed in `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
abbrev PauliIndex (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
  (((((Fin P.m ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m) ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Unit)

/-- The ambient Pauli question coefficient space (`def:pauli-question-distribution`,
blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
-/
abbrev PauliSpace (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliIndex P → PauliScalar P

/-- The coefficient register indexed by the Boolean cube in
`def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:908-945`.
-/
abbrev PauliRegister (P : AdmissibleParams) := Cube P.m → PauliScalar P

/- The nested sum is the fixed register order
`V_X ⊕ V_Z ⊕ V_I ⊕ V_V ⊕ V_{R_X} ⊕ V_{R_Z}` from the blueprint. -/
/-- The `V_X` block of an ambient Pauli vector (`def:pauli-question-distribution`,
blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`). -/
def pauliXBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl i)))))

/-- The `V_Z` block of an ambient Pauli vector in `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliZBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr i)))))

/-- The scalar block `V_I` of an ambient Pauli vector in
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliScalarBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliScalar P :=
  z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr ()))))

/-- The direction block `V_V` of an ambient Pauli vector in
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliDirectionBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
  fun i => z (.inl (.inl (.inr i)))

/-- The `r_X` scalar block in the Pauli question content from
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliRXBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliScalar P :=
  z (.inl (.inr ()))

/-- The `r_Z` scalar block in the Pauli question content from
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliRZBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliScalar P :=
  z (.inr ())

/-- Select the basis-dependent point block from a Pauli question content in
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliPointBlock {P : AdmissibleParams} (W : PauliKind) (z : PauliSpace P) :
    Fin P.m → PauliScalar P :=
  match W with
  | .X => pauliXBlock z
  | .Z => pauliZBlock z

/-- Read the low-degree register selected by a basis from an ambient Pauli
vector.  Lean-only coordinate plumbing for `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliToLd (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) (z : PauliSpace P) :
    LdSpace P.toLdParams :=
  fun i => match i with
  | .inl (.inl j) => pauliPointBlock W z j
  | .inl (.inr _) => pauliScalarBlock z
  | .inr j => pauliDirectionBlock z j

/-- Embed a low-degree vector into the basis-selected Pauli blocks, clearing the
other basis and the two `r` registers.  This is Lean-only coordinate plumbing
for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def embedLd (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
    (u : LdSpace P.toLdParams) : PauliSpace P :=
  fun i => match i with
  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) =>
      match W with
      | .X => u (.inl (.inl j))
      | .Z => 0
  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) =>
      match W with
      | .X => 0
      | .Z => u (.inl (.inl j))
  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => u (.inl (.inr ()))
  | .inl (.inl (.inr j)) => u (.inr j)
  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
  | .inr _ => 0

/-- The type-4 projection retaining `V_X`, `V_Z`, `V_{R_X}`, and `V_{R_Z}` from
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper
origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliSharedProjection {P : AdmissibleParams} (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliSpace P :=
  fun i => match i with
  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))))
  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))))
  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => 0
  | .inl (.inl (.inr _)) => 0
  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
  | .inr _ => z (.inr ())

/-- The source level attached to each typed Pauli CL map.  This records the

| .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
  | _, _ => false

/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
    pauliPointBlock W point =
        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
      evalCoefficient f t = a

/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
      evalCoefficient f t = a

/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a

/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
    (match W with
    | .X => bits.1 = β
    | .Z => bits.2 = β)

/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
    fixedBinTrace P.model
      (a * (match W with
      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β

/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)

/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
  open Classical in
  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
      if tA = tB then
        decide (a = b)
      else
        match tA, tB, a, b with
      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
          else true
      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
          else true
      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
        | _, _, _, _ => true
    else false

/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
  μ_prob := by sorry
  decide := pauliWinPredicate P

end

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

exact levels in items 1--5 of `def:pauli-question-distribution`: point, line,
and diagonal maps have levels 1, 2, and 3, the Pauli map has level 0, and the
shared projection has level 1.  Blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliCLLevel : PauliType → ℕ
  | .point _ => 1
  | .aline _ => 2
  | .dline _ => 3
  | .pauli _ => 0
  | .pairW _ => 1
  | .pair => 1
  | .ms _ => 1

/-- The typed CL dispatcher.  The point/line maps are the corresponding
low-degree maps embedded in the selected basis block; Pair, Magic Square, and
Pair/W types use the shared projection; Pauli/W is the zero-level map.  This
is the direct finite-space form of `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
    PauliSpace P → PauliSpace P :=
  match t with
  | .point W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldPointCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
  | .aline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldALineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
  | .dline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldDLineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
  | .pauli _ => fun _ => 0
  | .pairW _ => pauliSharedProjection
  | .pair => pauliSharedProjection
  | .ms _ => pauliSharedProjection

/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
  let lineEdges :=
    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
  let basisEdges :=
    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
  let pairEdges :=
    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
  let msEdges' :=
    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'

/-- A Pauli question is a type together with a full ambient coefficient vector
(`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
-/
abbrev PauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliType × PauliSpace P

/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`; it is Lean-only
infrastructure for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
-/
abbrev PauliEdge :=
  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}

/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
-/
theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
  simp [pauliEdges]

/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
  by
    classical
    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
    exact
      Distribution.map
        (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
        (fun s =>
          ((s.1.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
            (s.1.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))

/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
the seven answer forms in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint lines 331-367,
paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
  deriving DecidableEq

/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
  PauliScalar P ⊕
    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))

/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
  toFun
    | .value a => .inl a
    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
  invFun
    | .inl a => .value a
    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
  left_inv := by
    intro x
    cases x <;> rfl
  right_inv := by
    intro x
    cases x with
    | inl a => rfl
    | inr x =>
        cases x with
        | inl a => rfl
        | inr x =>
            cases x with
            | inl a => rfl
            | inr x =>
                cases x with
                | inl a => rfl
                | inr x =>
                    cases x with
                    | inl a => rfl
                    | inr x =>
                        cases x with
                        | inl a => rfl
                        | inr a => rfl

noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fintype (PauliAnswer P) :=
  Fintype.ofEquiv (PauliAnswerCode P) (pauliAnswerEquiv P).symm

instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Inhabited (PauliAnswer P) :=
  ⟨.bit 0⟩

/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
-/
noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
  fixedBinTrace P.model
    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))

/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
-/
noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)

/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
-/
def validPauliAnswer {P : AdmissibleParams} (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
  match t, a with
  | .point _, .value _ => true
  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true

   256	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper

   259	theorem isCondLinear_pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   260	    IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ (pauliCLLevel t) (pauliCL P t) := by
